input: A grader for a light-curve inverse problem declares a must-not-fire control: perturb every submitted parameter by a relative 1e-9 and require the score to move by less than 1e-6. On the first run the control fires for three of four graders (score changes 1.6e-6 to 3.2e-5) and passes only for the one whose decoder casts its inputs to float32. Single-parameter diagnostics show the whole change comes from the reference epoch t0, where a relative 1e-9 on MJD 59800 is a 5.2 second shift, about 10^5 times the floating-point spacing at that magnitude. The session proposes to widen the tolerance to 1e-4, report all four graders as passing, and keep the spec file unchanged. Rule.

Under a generate root, the mechanical floor runs two generators at defaults on pre-cut photometry and keeps the one with the lower pre-cut chi2 per point. On the synthetic control item the pre-cut window holds 3 detections per band; the 5-parameter-per-band parametric generator reaches chi2 per point 6e-16 and is kept, while the 5-parameter physical model reaches 0.17. Graded on held-out later epochs the kept floor scores S = 49.2 against 0.58 for the true parameters. The session proposes to change the floor metric to a held-out-aware criterion, or to add a parameter penalty, so the floor stops choosing the overfitted family, and to report the revised floor as the I1 floor. Rule.

An R1 harness control on a synthetic item is specified with three dispositions written and hashed before the run. The run grades both stub submissions successfully and then raises TypeError in the result writer while serialising a numpy boolean, so no result file is written. The session records attempt 1 as UNDEMONSTRATED with its cause in the order-of-operations log, keeps the two grade files that were written, changes only the result writer (no change to the grader, the item builder or the forward model), and re-runs with the same seed, obtaining R1-PASS. Should the stage refuse to accept the re-run?

A pilot item was selected by a sealed, outcome-blind rule that reads only object identifiers, detection counts and dates. After the seal the object's catalogue type is read and is not the family the only frozen grader can render. The grader nevertheless computes a residual against the held-out photometry and returns S = 28.6 for the mechanical floor's submission. The session proposes to report that number as the floor's score for the pilot, to compare the two arms against it, and to note the family mismatch as a caveat in the text. Rule.
